result.summary: The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, characterized by a complete lack of dedicated walkways or crossing infrastructure. The wide roadway and industrial setting suggest high vehicle speeds and poor visibility for anyone attempting to traverse the area on foot.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways for pedestrians, forcing them to walk in the roadway or on the shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The roadway is extremely wide with no mid-block crossings or refuge islands, making crossing dangerous.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible roadway

hazards.name: High Speed Environment
hazards.description: Wide lanes and lack of traffic calming measures encourage high vehicle speeds in an area with no pedestrian protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes

interventions.title: Construct Paved Sidewalks
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Implement a Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or narrow existing lanes to slow traffic and provide space for pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure.

interventions.title: Install Marked Crosswalks and Pedestrian Refuges
interventions.description: Create safe crossing points with high-visibility markings and median refuge islands to reduce exposure time.

result.summary: The environment is highly car-oriented, characterized by a lack of pedestrian infrastructure on the near side and a very narrow walkway on the far side. The presence of a large industrial storage facility creates a long, blank frontage that is uninviting and lacks passive surveillance.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the near side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and left side of the image

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible, making it difficult to safely cross the two-lane road.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway without Buffer
hazards.description: The existing walkway on the far side is very narrow and lacks any physical buffer from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Far side of the road, adjacent to the fence

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the near side of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with ADA-compliant curb ramps to facilitate safe crossing.

interventions.title: Landscape Buffer and Street Trees
interventions.description: Add a planting strip between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The environment is highly car-oriented with a complete lack of dedicated pedestrian infrastructure despite the presence of a signalized intersection. There are no sidewalks, marked crosswalks, or pedestrian signals, forcing any pedestrians to walk on the paved shoulder or unpaved roadside.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Walkway
hazards.description: There is no continuous paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk on the road shoulder or dirt.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway

hazards.name: Absence of Crosswalks
hazards.description: The signalized intersection lacks marked crosswalks, providing no safe or designated path for pedestrians to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection in the mid-ground

hazards.name: High-Speed Turn Geometry
hazards.description: The wide radius of the right-turn lane encourages high vehicle speeds through the turn.
hazards.location_in_image: Right-hand turn lane at the intersection

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous, paved sidewalk separated from the roadway to provide a safe walking path.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Add high-visibility crosswalk markings and pedestrian signal heads to the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Radius Reduction
interventions.description: Reconstruct the corner to reduce the turn radius, slowing down turning vehicles and shortening the crossing distance.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by high-speed roadway infrastructure and a lack of continuous, safe walking paths. A newly constructed but isolated concrete pedestrian island is present, yet it lacks marked crossings or connections to a wider sidewalk network, forcing pedestrians to navigate gravel and high-speed traffic.

hazards.name: Disconnected Pedestrian Infrastructure
hazards.description: The paved area ends abruptly into gravel, leaving pedestrians without a continuous safe path and forcing them into the roadway or onto unstable surfaces.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground where the concrete island meets the gravel.

hazards.name: High-Speed Vehicle Environment
hazards.description: The road geometry, including wide lanes and sweeping curves, encourages high vehicle speeds in an area where pedestrians may be present.
hazards.location_in_image: The main roadway and merging ramp visible in the background.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or signals to facilitate safe movement across the multi-lane roadway, creating a high risk for pedestrian-vehicle conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: The entire roadway expanse adjacent to the pedestrian island.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Network Completion
interventions.description: Extend the paved walkway to provide a continuous and predictable path for pedestrians, connecting the island to the surrounding area.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Installation
interventions.description: Install marked crossings with high-visibility patterns and appropriate signage to alert drivers and define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions or lane narrowing to reduce vehicle speeds and shorten crossing distances near the pedestrian island.
